title: G63 Max-Cut: a publicly verifiable solution of 27,050
description: A publicly verifiable Max-Cut configuration of value 27,050 for the G-set instance G63 (7,000 vertices, 41,459 unit-weight edges). Correction in version 1.1.0: version 1.0.0 described 27,050 as an improvement on the published 27,047 reference (arXiv:2510.21105) and stated that all verifiable primary sources listed at most 27,047 for G63. That was incorrect. An explicit, publicly verifiable G63 configuration with cut value 27,052 was published by R. Ota and M. Okada on 23 March 2026 (doi:10.5281/zenodo.19189885), Other researchers have also pointed us to earlier reports of 27,052 for the Fujitsu Digital Annealer (Matsubara et al., ASP-DAC 2020, doi:10.1109/ASP-DAC47756.2020.9045100; Takemoto et al., 2021, doi:10.14923/transelej.2020jci0010; no configuration published) and of 27,051 (Ju et al., IEEE Access 14, 2026, doi:10.1109/ACCESS.2026.3727846); we have not been able to verify these values in the full texts. 27,050 is therefore not the highest reported value for G63. It was found independently, from random initial states, with population annealing Monte Carlo on a consumer GPU (NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3060 Ti) on 8 November 2026. The record contains the full partition, SHA-256 checksums, dependency-free verifiers (Python, Node.js, awk), verification results, a structural comparison with the 27,047 configuration and a methodology description. No claim of optimality or of a new algorithm is made. The experiment was directed by the author; code, execution, verification tools and documentation drafts were produced with the AI assistant Claude (Anthropic). Data and documentation: CC BY 4.0; verifier code (verify/): MIT.
